lens: B — catch a false statement. No surfaces were named, so I chose them: the COVERAGE BOUNDARY heredoc printed by `scripts/test.sh` on every green run, `docs/session-state.md`'s current-state sections, `docs/v1-1-register.md` §9/§11, `docs/decisions.md` A-049/A-051/A-054/A-055/A-056, and `verifier/REPORT.md` F-6. Everything below was falsified by execution on the frozen worktree at 8234aba.

findings.title: The gate's own COVERAGE BOUNDARY quotes verifier counts of 149/62/24 and calls them "the floors this run asserts", 142 lines after the same run printed floors of 160/7/77/29
findings.claim: scripts/test.sh:523-525 prints "7/7 samples verify, 62/62 applicable tamper cases across 24 distinct modes behave as specified, and 149/149 of its own tests pass", and :534 asserts "ALL THREE FIGURES ARE FLOORS THIS RUN ASSERTS (A-047) — if the verifier shrinks, the gate fails and prints FLOOR BREACHED." All three quoted figures are false, and none of them is a floor this run asserts. The measured values are 7 samples, 77 tamper cases over 29 modes, 160 tests; the floors in the same file are VERIFIER_MIN_TESTS=160, VERIFIER_MIN_SAMPLES=7, VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER=77, VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER_MODES=29. A verifier that was exactly the size this block declares (149 tests, 62 cases, 24 modes) would FAIL the gate with FLOOR BREACHED, so the sentence is false in the one direction that matters. A-054 (154→158), A-055 (tamper 62→68, 24→25 modes) and A-056 (158→160, 68→77, 25→29) each moved the numbers and none rewrote this block, even though its own maintenance note says it "is ONE statement, not a running log… When a step lands, REWRITE the affected layer below. Do not append."
findings.why_it_matters: This is the exact defect A-045/A-047 were written to close, reproduced inside the paragraph that narrates them: the same block says four lines earlier that A-045 left "the figures … quoted prose beside a run that produced different ones" and that a reviewer got "Ran 145 tests" and "146/146 of its own tests pass" in one green run. Nothing in test.sh reconciles the heredoc prose to the stage line, so the reconciliation gap the floors were supposed to close is still open one level up — the floors defend the run, nothing defends the sentence about the run. The block is explicitly the artifact a reader is told to consult instead of the pass count ("read this, not the pass count"), and its wording is the source text that has repeatedly been copied into session-state and the gate packs.
findings.reproduction:
cd <scratchpad>/r5/b-claims
./scripts/test.sh > /tmp/baseline.log 2>&1; echo EXIT=$?   # EXIT=0
grep -n 'floor 160\|GATE PASSED' /tmp/baseline.log
#  1151:  suite 160 (floor 160) · verdict clean · samples 7 (floor 7) · tamper 77 cases / 29 modes (floors 77/29)
#  1153: GATE PASSED
sed -n '1293,1295p' /tmp/baseline.log
#  ... 7/7 samples verify, 62/62
#  applicable tamper cases across 24 distinct modes behave as specified, and 149/149
#  of its own tests pass.
grep -n 'ALL THREE FIGURES ARE FLOORS' /tmp/baseline.log   # present, ~line 1302
grep -n 'VERIFIER_MIN_' scripts/test.sh
#  248:VERIFIER_MIN_TESTS=160   249:VERIFIER_MIN_SAMPLES=7   250:VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER=77   262:VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER_MODES=29

Independent second measurement, not via test.sh:
python3 -B -c "import io,os,sys,unittest; sys.path.insert(0,os.path.join(os.getcwd(),'verifier')); r=unittest.TextTestRunner(stream=io.StringIO(),verbosity=0).run(unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromName('test_verifier')); print(r.testsRun, len(r.skipped), len(r.failures), len(r.errors))"
#  160 0 0 0
python3 -B verifier/verify.py --all fixtures/samples | tail -1        # 7/7 sample(s) verified
python3 -B verifier/verify.py --all fixtures/samples --tamper all > /tmp/t.txt
grep -c 'tamper self-test PASS' /tmp/t.txt                            # 77
grep -oE 'the mutated [a-z-]+' /tmp/t.txt | sed 's/the mutated //' | sort -u | wc -l   # 29
findings.probe_moved_something: The gate run itself was the probe and it moved three of the four numbers away from the prose in a single output: the stage line at log:1151 reads 160/7/77/29 while the heredoc at log:1293-1295 reads 149/7/62/24. I then re-derived 160 / 7 / 77 / 29 by running the three arms standalone outside test.sh, so the disagreement is not an artefact of the script's parsing. Both measurements agree with each other and disagree with the prose.

findings.title: The COVERAGE BOUNDARY states "No mutation sweep has been run over verify.py itself, which is 1681 lines" — it was swept (A-055) and the file is 1830 lines
findings.claim: The gate prints, on every green run: "No mutation sweep has been run over `verify.py` itself, which is 1681 lines and DECIDES the verdict." Both halves are false. `verify.py` was swept on 2026-08-17 — `docs/v1-1-register.md` §11 is titled "The `verify.py` sweep, 2026-08-17 (A-055) — 14 survivors, 2 LIVE defects, 3 closed", and the sweep's remediation is in the tree (the `_find_domain` trust-root rework and the named check "the trust root is the deployment's, not the presenter's", plus the `receipt-wrongkey` tamper mode). The file is 1830 lines, not 1681. `docs/v1-1-register.md` §9 carries the same false sentence in the present tense — "And `verify.py` — 1681 lines, the file that actually decides PASS or FAIL — was not swept. That is now the largest measured gap in the verifier." — two sections above §11, which records the sweep.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a coverage claim, not a count: it tells the reader that the file deciding PASS/FAIL has never been mutation-tested, in the one artifact designated as the statement of what is and is not covered. It understates coverage, which sounds harmless, but the cost is concrete — it erases the actual current state, which is 13-14 recorded latent survivors in `verify.py` clustering on the override stage (register §11), several closed by A-056 and two deliberately left open. A reader planning the next round from the boundary would commission a sweep that has already run, and would not see the survivor list that is the real residue. The register having the same sentence in §9 while §11 contradicts it also means the standing brief's "known findings" map is self-contradicting on exactly this point.
findings.reproduction:
cd <scratchpad>/r5/b-claims
wc -l verifier/verify.py
#  1830 verifier/verify.py            <- boundary says 1681
grep -n 'No mutation sweep has been' scripts/test.sh          # 556
grep -n '^## 11' docs/v1-1-register.md
#  474:## 11. The `verify.py` sweep, 2026-08-17 (A-055) — 14 survivors, 2 LIVE defects, 3 closed
sed -n '452,453p' docs/v1-1-register.md
#  ...`verify.py` — 1681 lines ... — was not swept.** That is now the largest measured gap in the verifier.

The sweep's output is in the tree, so it demonstrably ran:
grep -n "the trust root is the deployment's, not the presenter's" verifier/verify.py   # 196
grep -n '_find_domain' verifier/verify.py                                              # 88, 184
grep -n 'receipt-wrongkey' verifier/verify.py                                          # 138, 209, 225

And it is printed by the gate:
grep -n 'No mutation sweep has been' /tmp/baseline.log        # 1326
findings.probe_moved_something: `wc -l` moved the number 1681 -> 1830 (a 149-line delta, i.e. the claim is not a rounding). The grep for `receipt-wrongkey` and the trust-root check name returned live line numbers inside the very file the sentence says was never swept — those identifiers exist only because the sweep ran, so the probe produced positive evidence rather than an absence.

findings.title: The COVERAGE BOUNDARY says RFC 8785's number and code-unit-ordering paths "are untested by anything (REPORT.md F-6)" — both are tested, in the suite this same gate runs, and REPORT.md says something different and correct
findings.surface: scripts/test.sh lines 568-570 (COVERAGE BOUNDARY, D-010 LIMIT); cites verifier/REPORT.md F-6
findings.claim: The gate prints: "The corpus exercises no JSON numbers and no non-ASCII, so RFC 8785's number and code-unit-ordering paths — its two most error-prone branches — are untested by anything (REPORT.md F-6)." Falsified twice by directed mutation: `verifier/test_verifier.py` contains `TestJCSNumbers.test_number_serialization` (13 RFC 8785 appendix-B number vectors) and `TestJCSStructure.test_key_sorting_is_utf16_code_units`, and both are inside the 160 tests the D-010 gate stage runs. Worse, the cited source says the opposite: REPORT.md's summary line reads "**RFC 8785's number and non-ASCII paths are unexercised by the corpus** (F-6) — this implementation is pinned to the RFC's vectors; agreement with the *evaluator* on those paths is untested by anything, because no fixture reaches them." The boundary dropped the subject ("agreement with the evaluator") and kept the predicate ("untested by anything"), inverting a correctly-scoped limitation into a false one. The same boundary paragraph contradicts itself 45 lines earlier: "its keccak is pinned to published vectors and its JCS to RFC 8785's appendix-B vectors, so green means agreement with the STANDARD, not with itself." The test class docstring says it too: "None of these are exercised by the Sentinel fixtures … They are tested anyway because the schema does not forbid a real number appearing later."
findings.why_it_matters: This is precisely the shape the lens names as round two's worst finding — a statement about a statement that misdescribes the one document that stated the limitation correctly — and it has reached the artifact the project treats as canonical. Two costs, in opposite directions. It understates what the verifier tests (a future reviewer writes tests that exist, or a maintainer deletes them believing nothing depended on them). And it deletes the real gap: the recorded limitation is about cross-implementation agreement between `verifier/jcs.py` and `ts/src/evaluate/jcs.ts`, which is the whole point of D-010's independence claim, and that gap now appears nowhere in the boundary at all. It is also load-bearing in a specific way: `ts/src/evaluate/jcs.ts` THROWS on any JSON number and rejects non-ASCII keys, while `verifier/jcs.py` accepts and serialises both — the two implementations are not merely uncompared on those paths, they have different acceptance sets. The boundary's wording hides that entirely.
findings.reproduction:
cd <scratchpad>/r5/b-claims
cp verifier/jcs.py /tmp/jcs.orig; rm -rf verifier/__pycache__

# CLEAN BASELINE (note: PYTHONPATH is required; without it unittest errors and a probe reads dead)
PYTHONPATH=verifier python3 -B -m unittest test_verifier.TestJCSNumbers test_verifier.TestJCSStructure 2>&1 | tail -3
#  Ran 9 tests in 0.002s
#  OK

# PROBE 1 — sort keys by code point instead of UTF-16 code units
sed -i '' 's|    return key.encode("utf-16-be", errors="surrogatepass")|    return key  # MUTANT|' verifier/jcs.py
git diff --stat -- verifier/jcs.py     # 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)   <- edit applied
rm -rf verifier/__pycache__
PYTHONPATH=verifier python3 -B -m unittest test_verifier.TestJCSStructure 2>&1 | tail -6
#  - {"�":1,"\U0001f600":2}
#  + {"\U0001f600":2,"�":1}
#  Ran 7 tests ... FAILED (failures=1)     <- test_key_sorting_is_utf16_code_units
cp /tmp/jcs.orig verifier/jcs.py; rm -rf verifier/__pycache__

# PROBE 2 — widen the ECMAScript number threshold 21 -> 22
sed -i '' 's|    if k <= n <= 21:|    if k <= n <= 22:  # MUTANT|' verifier/jcs.py
git diff --stat -- verifier/jcs.py     # 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)
rm -rf verifier/__pycache__
PYTHONPATH=verifier python3 -B -m unittest test_verifier.TestJCSNumbers 2>&1 | tail -8
#  AssertionError: '1000000000000000000000' != '1e+21'
#  Ran 2 tests ... FAILED (failures=1)     <- test_number_serialization
cp /tmp/jcs.orig verifier/jcs.py; rm -rf verifier/__pycache__
git diff --stat -- verifier/jcs.py      # empty — tree restored
PYTHONPATH=verifier python3 -B -m unittest test_verifier 2>&1 | tail -3    # Ran 160 tests ... OK

The cited source, in full:
sed -n '1087,1089p' verifier/REPORT.md
sed -n '143,150p' verifier/test_verifier.py    # the class docstring saying the opposite
findings.probe_moved_something: Two independent mutations each turned a green targeted run into a failing one, with the diff text printed (`{"\U0001f600":2,"�":1}` vs the expected order; `'1000000000000000000000' != '1e+21'`), and the clean tree ran 9/9 OK before and 160/160 OK after restore. My FIRST attempt at the baseline was dead — `python3 -m unittest test_verifier` without PYTHONPATH gives ModuleNotFoundError and reads as 2 errors on a clean tree — so I discarded it and re-ran with a passing clean baseline before believing either failure. Also worth noting for precision: A-051 recorded that this sorting test's witness pair orders identically under UTF-16 BE and LE, so the test cannot catch a BE->LE swap; it does catch a code-point sort, which is the mutation the boundary's sentence is about. Both facts are true and neither makes "untested by anything" true.

findings.title: docs/session-state.md §5's D-010 bullet still reads 7/7, 62/62, 24 modes, 149/149 and calls all four floors — contradicting its own §3 headline 79 lines above, at the exact line whose in-place annotation narrates this happening twice before
findings.surface: docs/session-state.md line 247 (§5 D-010 bullet), versus line 168 (§3 headline)
findings.claim: session-state.md:168 states "**73/73 Foundry · 405/405 TypeScript · 160/160 verifier · 77 tamper cases over 29 modes · 50 corpus fixtures · 7 samples …**". session-state.md:247 states "**D-010 verifier:** 7/7 samples, 62/62 applicable tamper cases over 24 distinct modes, 149/149 tests — **and all four are now FLOORS the gate asserts (A-047), not prose.**" The second is false on three of four numbers and false on the floors claim. The file contradicts itself, in the file whose first paragraph says "**This file, not the conversation, is the memory.** If it disagrees with anything an agent remembers, this file wins." The italic annotation attached to line 247 is the aggravating fact: it says this same line read `6/6, 42/42, 70/70` while the §3 headline already said 146/146, that it "was **not** fixed by A-045, whose decision entry and commit message both claim 'both layers are corrected'; exactly one was", and that it was found by an independent reviewer rather than the author. That is the third occurrence of one defect at one line, the second time it was the site left behind while the headline was swept.
findings.why_it_matters: The reading order at session-state.md:16-22 sends a fresh instance to §0 and §1, then to the decision log; §3 and §5 are the current-state block a resuming agent quotes from. §3 carries a warning to re-verify before quoting; §5 carries no such warning and carries the stronger sentence ("all four are now FLOORS the gate asserts, not prose"), which is exactly the sentence that stops someone re-measuring. This is the site from which the stale figures have historically been copied into gate packs, and it is the recorded pattern — a fix that generalises the demonstration (sweep the headline) instead of the argument (sweep every site that carries the figure) — recurring at the same line for the third time.
findings.reproduction:
cd <scratchpad>/r5/b-claims
sed -n '168,169p' docs/session-state.md
#  **73/73 Foundry · 405/405 TypeScript · 160/160 verifier · 77 tamper cases over 29 modes ·
sed -n '247,248p' docs/session-state.md
#  - **D-010 verifier:** 7/7 samples, 62/62 applicable tamper cases over 24 distinct modes, 149/149 tests — **and all four
#    are now FLOORS the gate asserts (A-047), not prose.**

Measured values (see B-1 for the commands): 160 tests, 7 samples, 77 tamper cases, 29 modes.
Floors actually asserted: grep -n 'VERIFIER_MIN_' scripts/test.sh -> 160 / 7 / 77 / 29.
So §3 is right, §5 is wrong, and the two are 79 lines apart in one file.
findings.probe_moved_something: The same two independent measurements as B-1 (the gate stage line at baseline.log:1151, and the standalone re-derivation 160/7/77/29) contradict line 247 while agreeing with line 168 — so the probe discriminates between the two sites rather than failing against both, which is what shows it is live.

findings.title: decisions.md A-055 claims "Suite 154 → 158" — its commit added zero test methods; A-054, its parent, made that transition and claims it too
findings.surface: docs/decisions.md, entry A-055 (2026-08-17), the sentence "Suite 154 → 158, tamper 62 → 68 over 25 modes"; compare entry A-054's "Suite 154 → 158"
findings.claim: Two consecutive decision entries claim the same suite growth. Measured against the commits: 75375b3 (A-051) = 154 test methods; 6b4d213 (A-054) = 158; 3bb4b21 (A-055) = 158; 4bc5d44 (A-056) = 160. A-055's commit changed `verifier/test_verifier.py` by +6/-1 lines and those lines are a single constant (`self.assertEqual(exercised, 48…)` → `54`) plus a comment — no new test method. So A-055 grew the suite by 0 and its "Suite 154 → 158" attributes A-054's +4 to itself. A-055's tamper half is correct and is its own work (`VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER` 62→68 and `VERIFIER_MIN_TAMPER_MODES` 24→25 are the only floor edits in that commit; `VERIFIER_MIN_TESTS=158` appears in the diff only as context, i.e. A-055 did not raise it).
findings.why_it_matters: The suite delta is offered inside A-055 as corroboration that the remediation landed — it sits in the same sentence as "Falsified: that same neutering now fails the suite and the tamper arm." A reader reconciling the decision log's figures against the tree gets 146→149→154→158 (A-054) →158 (A-055, claiming 154→158) →160, i.e. one transition claimed twice and 162 if summed. `decisions.md` is the record John's rulings are read from, and A-051 already recorded one instance of `decisions.md` being the single site that carried a false restatement after the code and register were corrected. This is a second instance of the same file being the wrong one. It also matters for the `receipt-wrongkey` mode specifically: the entry implies test coverage was added for it, and the +0 shows the mode is covered only by the loop-driven tamper arm and the bumped count constant — no structural test names it, consistent with A-051's note that only `evidence-hash` has one.
findings.reproduction:
cd <scratchpad>/r5/b-claims
grep -cE '^\s+def test_' verifier/test_verifier.py          # 160  (matches testsRun=160, so the proxy is calibrated)
for c in 75375b3 6b4d213 3bb4b21 4bc5d44; do echo -n "$c -> "; git show $c:verifier/test_verifier.py | grep -cE '^\s+def test_'; done
#  75375b3 -> 154     (A-051)
#  6b4d213 -> 158     (A-054)
#  3bb4b21 -> 158     (A-055)   <- claims "Suite 154 -> 158"
#  4bc5d44 -> 160     (A-056)
git log --format='%h %p %s' -1 3bb4b21          # parent is 6b4d213, i.e. A-054 landed first
git diff 6b4d213 3bb4b21 -- verifier/test_verifier.py
#  only: -self.assertEqual(exercised, 48, ...)  +self.assertEqual(exercised, 54, ...) plus 5 comment lines
git diff 6b4d213 3bb4b21 -- scripts/test.sh
#  VERIFIER_MIN_TESTS=158 appears as CONTEXT (unchanged); only TAMPER 62->68 and MODES 24->25 change
findings.probe_moved_something: The per-commit method counts moved across the four commits (154 / 158 / 158 / 160) and the flat step is exactly at A-055 — so the count is discriminating, not constant. The proxy was calibrated first: the current tree's 160 `def test_` matches the executed `testsRun=160`, so counting definitions is measuring the same quantity the entry names. The diff of A-055's own commit shows the flatness directly rather than being inferred from the count.

findings.title: docs/session-state.md's header says "Last updated: 2026-08-16, end of session" while the commit it names and every entry it summarises are 2026-08-17
findings.claim: Line 6 reads "Last updated: **2026-08-16**, end of session. Branch `step-3/isolated-signer`, **pushed** (`4166ff0`…)." Commit 4166ff0 is authored 2026-08-17 ("Handoff: rewrite session-state for a fresh instance"), as are the five commits before it. The file's own reading order at line 18 tells a fresh instance to read "D-045 through D-048 and A-045 through A-056, which is the 2026-08-16/17 hardening arc", and §3's annotation refers to figures being stale "until 2026-08-17" — so the body knows the date the header does not. The file has a self-warning about the commit pointer trailing by one doc-only commit; that warning covers the hash, not the date.
findings.why_it_matters: Small, but the date is how a resuming agent decides whether the current-state block is worth re-measuring. A file that declares itself the memory and reports being a day older than it is biases the reader toward "this was written after everything I am about to read" being false. It is also the same file that carries B-4's stale D-010 bullet, so the two compound: an agent that trusts the date has less reason to re-verify the counts.
findings.reproduction:
cd <scratchpad>/r5/b-claims
sed -n '6,7p' docs/session-state.md
#  Last updated: **2026-08-16**, end of session. Branch `step-3/isolated-signer`, **pushed**
#  (`4166ff0`, verified against the remote rather than trusting the push output). ...
git log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=short -6
#  8234aba 2026-08-17 session-state: advance the pointer
#  4166ff0 2026-08-17 Handoff: rewrite session-state for a fresh instance
#  a590b03 2026-08-17 D-048 ... 4bc5d44 2026-08-17 A-056 ... 3bb4b21 2026-08-17 A-055
findings.probe_moved_something: `git log --date=short` returned 2026-08-17 for the exact commit hash the line quotes (4166ff0) — the probe resolved the file's own named referent rather than a nearby one, and the returned date differs from the stated one.

findings.title: session-state.md tells a fresh instance that gate-s2-evidence.md §11 "is now empty" 22 lines after telling it to read §11 before repeating any claim — §11 has six entries, five of them live
findings.surface: docs/session-state.md line 43-44, versus line 21 and docs/gate-s2-evidence.md §11
findings.claim: session-state.md:21 says "`docs/gate-s2-evidence.md` §11 is what is NOT in evidence — read it before repeating any claim about what this project has proven." session-state.md:43-44 then says "**The steps 1–3 review S2 was signed WITHOUT has since been run (D-044(b)), and §11 is now empty.**" §11 of the pack is not empty: it carries six bullets, of which one (the steps 1-3 review) is struck through and five are live, including "Verdict correctness in general", "A live agent in CI" and "The evidence dashboard". The charitable reading — that the §11 ENTRY for that one review is now emptied — is available and is probably what was meant; I am reporting it because the sentence as written says the opposite of line 21 and of the pack's own §11 preamble ("a gate pack that only lists what it has is the failure mode §7.5 exists to prevent"), and because §11 is precisely the document that round two's worst finding misdescribed.
findings.why_it_matters: The two sentences are 22 lines apart in the file a fresh instance reads first, and they give opposite instructions about the same section: read it, and it is empty. An agent that takes the second reading skips the pack's statement of what Sentinel has NOT proven — which is the single document the project most relies on to prevent overclaiming. Cheap to fix with four words ("and that §11 entry is now struck through").
findings.reproduction:
cd <scratchpad>/r5/b-claims
sed -n '21p;43,44p' docs/session-state.md
sed -n "$(grep -n '^## 11' docs/gate-s2-evidence.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1),+12p" docs/gate-s2-evidence.md
#  ## 11. What is NOT in evidence
#  - **Verdict correctness in general.** ...
#  - **A live agent in CI.** ...
#  - **The evidence dashboard** ...
#  - ~~**An independent review of §9 steps 1-3.**~~ **RUN 2026-08-16 ...**
awk '/^## 11\./,/^## 12\./' docs/gate-s2-evidence.md | grep -c '^- \*\*'    # 6
findings.probe_moved_something: The bullet count returned 6, not 0 — the probe produced a positive integer against a claim of emptiness rather than an absence of output, and the struck-through bullet is visibly one of the six, which is what makes the charitable reading identifiable rather than assumed.

brief_critique:
The lens brief's decision to name no surfaces was correct and load-bearing. My three best findings are inside a bash heredoc in `scripts/test.sh` — neither a document nor executable code, and a surface list written by someone thinking in terms of "docs / code / tests" would very likely not have contained it. Keep that choice.

The standing brief's baseline line ("160 verifier (floor 160) · … 77 tamper cases over 29 modes") was accurate and is what made this round cheap: it let me spot the 149/62/24 in the gate's own output within the first twenty minutes. That line is doing real work; do not compress it.

Two defects in the standing brief, both of the kind it asks me to name.

1. **It points at `docs/v1-1-register.md` as the map of known-and-deliberately-unfixed findings and warns that re-reporting one is not a finding — but that file is self-contradicting on the exact point of B-2.** §9 ends "And `verify.py` — 1681 lines … — was not swept. That is now the largest measured gap in the verifier", in the present tense; §11, 22 sections-worth of text later, is titled "The `verify.py` sweep, 2026-08-17 (A-055)". A reviewer using the register as its map of already-covered ground can be told, in the present tense, that the largest gap is open when it is closed. If the register is going to be handed to reviewers as a known-findings list, either each section needs an "as of <date>, superseded by §N" stamp or §9's closing sentence needs the correction §11 implies. As it stands the brief's own instrument points at a stale claim.

2. **The environment section warns about `__pycache__`, the Foundry PATH and Node's type stripping, but not about the verifier suite's import path — and that omission produced exactly the dead probe the brief warns about.** `python3 -m unittest test_verifier` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'test_verifier'` unless `verifier/` is on `sys.path` (test.sh does `sys.path.insert` inline). My first clean baseline for B-3 came back "FAILED (errors=2)" on an untouched tree; had I run the mutation first and compared to nothing, both mutations would have "failed" for a reason unrelated to the code and I would have reported a live test as dead. One line — "run the verifier suite as `PYTHONPATH=verifier python3 -B -m unittest test_verifier`, or `python3 -B verifier/test_verifier.py`" — belongs next to the `__pycache__` note, since it is the same class of trap and the brief already spends a paragraph on that class.

One smaller note: the brief says "Prefer targeted runs … Run the full gate only when a finding actually needs it." For lens B specifically, the full gate IS the instrument — the COVERAGE BOUNDARY heredoc only ever appears on a green full run, and three of my seven findings live in it. A lens-B brief should say so explicitly, or a reviewer following the efficiency guidance will never see the text that carries the round's best material.

Then two directed mutations of `verifier/jcs.py` (`_sort_key` → code-point order; number threshold `21`→`22`), each with a passing clean baseline before and a verified-empty `git diff` after, `python3 -B` with `verifier/__pycache__` removed between every variant per the brief. No `commit`, `push`, `checkout <branch>`, or `worktree`. No network. No process killed — 17 `anvil`/`forge` processes belonging to other sessions were visible and left alone. Nothing under `<repo>` was read, written or executed; every path I touched is under the worktree or the session scratchpad.

**What I read.** `scripts/test.sh` in full; `check-type-strings.sh`, `check-eval-codes.sh`, `check-label-prompt.sh` in full; `verifier/jcs.py` (partial), `verifier/verify.py` (greps only), `verifier/test_verifier.py` lines 140-200 plus greps; `ts/src/signer/eip712.ts` (first 120 lines), `ts/src/signer/protocol.ts` (partial), `ts/src/evaluate/jcs.ts` (greps); `docs/session-state.md` §0/§3/§5 regions; `docs/v1-1-register.md` §1, §9, §10, §11 and its heading list; `docs/decisions.md` entries A-049, A-051, A-054, A-055, A-056; `verifier/REPORT.md` around F-6 and its summary list; `docs/gate-s2-evidence.md` §11 only; `README.md`, `Sentinel_Protocol_Lab_Proposal_v0_2.md` §5.8 lines only.

**Injected context that did not come from this brief or the worktree — it happened, and I am naming it.** The harness prepended (a) `$HOME/Projects/CLAUDE.md`, the workspace instruction file, and (b) `$HOME/.claude/projects/.../memory/MEMORY.md`, a user auto-memory file [redacted before publication: personal context, 2026-09-05] with a multi-line Sentinel summary (gate status, D-047/D-048, "start every session at Sentinel/docs/session-state.md §1"), plus MCP-server instruction blocks, a skills catalogue and periodic "task tools haven't been used" reminders. **Influence: none on any finding.** Every finding is grounded in a file inside the worktree and a command I ran there; I did not use MEMORY.md's Sentinel summary as evidence for anything, and I deliberately did not follow its "start at `Sentinel/docs/session-state.md`" pointer, which names the live tree I am forbidden to read — I read the worktree's copy instead. CLAUDE.md's Godot/MCP rules were irrelevant; its "do not write report/summary/findings .md files" rule I did follow (no report file was written; the only files I created are `baseline.log`, `jcs.py.orig` and two greps' output, all in the scratchpad, none in the worktree).

**Instructions encountered inside files and declined.** None directed at me. I did not open `fixtures/injection/`, `fixtures/corpus/` view files or the spike transcripts, which is where the brief says the adversarial text lives — so I encountered no injection attempt, and that is an absence of exposure rather than a successful resistance. `scripts/test.sh` and the register contain many imperative sentences ("Raise a floor when the suite genuinely grows; NEVER lower one", "If this fails, add the check to §5.7.1"); I treated all of them as data about the project's intent, and changed nothing in the tree.

**Claimed without executing.** Three things. (i) That A-054 and A-055 were concurrent sessions is read from A-054's prose ("done while the `verify.py` sweep runs"), not measured — B-5 does not depend on it, since the git parentage and the +0 method delta stand alone. (ii) In B-3 I state that `ts/src/evaluate/jcs.ts` throws on numbers and rejects non-ASCII keys; I read that from the source and its error strings, I did not run the TypeScript to confirm it. (iii) In B-1 I assert that a verifier at 149/62/24 would fail the gate; that follows from the printed floors (160/7/77/29) by arithmetic — I did not shrink the suite to 149 and re-run the gate to watch FLOOR BREACHED print, so that one specific sentence is inference from an executed measurement rather than a second execution.

**Where I ran out of budget.** The deep profile (`./scripts/test.sh --gate`) was never run, so the §7.1 corpus stage, the committed-view file-by-file check, the `EXPECTED_NORM` pin and the ablation figures are unverified by me — including session-state's "gate green at the deep profile".
coverage_statement:
**Swept, with execution.** The `COVERAGE BOUNDARY` heredoc in `scripts/test.sh` (lines ~490-660) sentence by sentence against measurement — this is where five of seven findings sit, and I checked every quantitative claim in it that I could reach on the fast profile: the D-010 counts (160/7/77/29 — three false), the floors claim (false), the verify.py-sweep claim (false), the line count (false), the JCS "untested by anything" claim (false, by two mutations), 41 declared conformance checks (true), 33 declared signer checks (true), 6 type strings (true), 14/20 classes and 39/43 fixtures (both true, matched to the guard's live output), 73 Foundry and 405 TypeScript (true). `docs/session-state.md` §3 and §5's current-state figures against the same measurements. `docs/decisions.md` A-049/A-051/A-054/A-055/A-056's suite and tamper deltas against per-commit method counts from git. `verifier/REPORT.md` F-6 and its summary line against the boundary's citation of it.

**Looked at, not swept.** `docs/v1-1-register.md` — I read §1, §9, §10, §11 and the heading list, and checked §9/§11 against each other; §§2-8 and §12 I did not audit, so any false claim in the eight sections covering the corpus, the vault, the §2 capability table and the eight guard defects is untouched by this round. `docs/gate-s2-evidence.md` — I opened §11 only, ~40 lines of 667; the other 620 lines of a signed evidence pack are unexamined, and the lens brief specifically flags signed packs as where round two's worst finding landed. `verifier/REPORT.md` — F-6's region and the summary list only, ~60 lines of 1265.

**Not opened at all.** `docs/gate-s1-evidence.md`, `docs/gate-5-vendor-audit.md` (502 lines, and Gate 5 is where two false claims were found in an earlier round), `docs/ablation-report.md`, `docs/review-2026-08-15/`, `HANDOFF.md` (greps only), and all but a few greps of the 79k-word proposal. `scripts/check-secrets.sh`, `check-class-coverage.sh` (447 lines), `check-vendor-honesty.sh` (407 lines), `check-rename-gate.sh` and `scripts/mutate.sh` (1032 lines) — I read their claims as printed in the baseline output and as described in test.sh's stage comments, but I did not read their source, so any guard whose printed line overstates what its code does is a live hole this lens did not probe. `fixtures/` in its entirety, including the corpus views, the labeller files and the injection material. All 83 TypeScript test suites and all 5 Foundry suites: I confirmed they pass and confirmed three counts, and verified nothing about what any individual test asserts. Commit messages, which the lens names as an in-scope surface, I checked only as one-line `git log` subjects — the bodies are unread, and A-045's commit message is already on record as having carried a false "both layers are corrected".

**Null results worth recording as measured rather than skipped.** `check-type-strings.sh`'s six-of-six claim holds and there is no seventh signed type it omits (`RefusalRecord` is deliberately not EIP-712 — verified in `eip712.ts`). The §9 s3 "33 declared checks" and §9 s6 "41 declared checks" figures are current. `check-eval-codes.sh` greps the whole proposal rather than §5.7.1, but that is already register §8.1 and I am not re-reporting it.

**Direction I did not take.** This lens hunts statements; I spent it almost entirely on current-state figures and coverage claims, which is where the last four rounds' hits were. I did not attempt the other half of the lens — a claim about what a *layer* proves that is wider than what that layer runs, e.g. the §9 s1/s2/s4/s5 paragraphs about the vault, the decoders and the Anvil pipeline. Those four layers' limit statements are asserted and unchecked by anything I ran, and a reviewer taking the same lens next round should start there rather than repeating this sweep.
